@graph.name: 25 open-source task managers compared (2026) · todoi.org
@graph.description: Licence, features and six scored criteria for open-source and source-available task managers, each with the reasoning attached.

acceptedAnswer.text: A volunteer-run directory of twenty-five browser-based task managers whose source you can read. Every score includes its reasoning. Nothing to sign up for, and no project pays to be listed.

mainEntity.name: Why is community size a category rather than a number?

acceptedAnswer.text: Stars, forks, contributors, cadence and forum activity measure different things, and none of them is a deployment count. Redmine sits in the top band on 6.0k stars because GitHub holds a mirror; Plane sits there on 59.5k. Both figures are accurate. Neither is an install count.

mainEntity.name: Why are the integration counts estimates?

acceptedAnswer.text: They count documented connectors, importers and plugins. API and webhook access is listed separately, because that describes what you could build rather than a ready-made connection.

mainEntity.name: Are all twenty-five assessed to the same depth?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The Confidence value on every record says which. The original eleven were read twice. The fourteen added on 17 September 2026 are a first pass - most of them Medium. If you find an error, send a correction with a source.

mainEntity.name: Does a project have to be self-hostable to be listed?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The rules are a browser interface and open, or partly open, source. Most entries are servers you run yourself. Logseq, Super Productivity and Taskwarrior are here because local files are another way to keep control.
Compiled on 17 September 2026; each record notes what was changing. Nextcloud announced Gantt for Deck in June 2026. The hosted Huly service shut down around 20 July 2026; self-hosting continued.

@graph.name: Open-source and source-available browser-based task managers, 2026
@graph.description: Twenty-five browser-based open-source and source-available task and project management projects, each assessed across 43 fields: licensing model, community proxy, repository stars, estimated integrations, five capability checks, deployment, calendar sync, data-out routes, stack and hosted option, plus six editorial 1-5 criteria, each carrying a written justification and a source list.
@graph.measurementTechnique: Editorial assessment of project documentation, source repositories and release histories against six published criteria.

variableMeasured.name: Ease of deployment
variableMeasured.description: Containers and packages, dependency count, operational complexity, upgrade burden and the state of the documentation.

variableMeasured.name: Ease of use
variableMeasured.description: Interface clarity, learning curve, conceptual overhead and whether non-specialists can live in it.

variableMeasured.name: Enterprise features
variableMeasured.description: Permissions, identity, audit and governance, portfolio reporting, scalability and administration.

variableMeasured.name: Interface flexibility
variableMeasured.description: How many genuinely useful views exist, plus workflow and custom-field options, dashboards, filters and extension points.

variableMeasured.name: Data sovereignty
variableMeasured.description: Whether you can run it independently, read its source, and keep control of the application and its data infrastructure.

variableMeasured.name: Portability
variableMeasured.description: APIs and exports, conventional storage and database choices, licensing constraints, and how realistically you could leave.
